newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The rand started off the new year on an uneasy note, reaching another historic low of 8.0178 against the British currency and shedding 1.2 cents against the dollar, as it was caught in the crossfire between the stronger major currencies.
- Money supply and private credit extension growth dropped in November to levels below what economists had predicted, signalling that a slowdown could be under way in response to high interest rates
- The Mozambique government has granted South African mining house JCI Ltd a 120-day option to lead manage the development of a $1.5 billion coking coal project in Moatize in central Mozambique.

- Weigh-Less Health and Slimming clubs founder chairman Mary Holroyd said on Thursday she would settle the impending legal action brought against her by Weight Watchers International, smoothing the way for the U.S.-based company's return to South Africa.

- Captain Hansie Cronje's men rode their early luck on the opening day of the second cricket test against India at Newlands on Thursday, and by the close were in a commanding position of 280 for four wickets.
- A Worcester Magistrate's Court security guard may be the vital link to an escaped right-wing death squad wanted in connection with the Christmas Eve shopping centre blasts in the Boland town.
- The rand hit a record low of eight-to-one against the British pound on Thursday. In the first trading session of 1997 it fell to 8.0269 against sterling.

- The holiday death toll on South Africa's roads passed the 1,000 mark on Thursday, with the National Traffic Information Centre reporting that 1,016 people had been killed since the start of the holiday season on December 3.

- The average national matric exam pass rate of 52.2 percent was an improvement on last year's performance, but Education Minister Sibusiso Bengu has hinted at changes in the way future matrics will be assessed.
- Two illgal immigrants were eaten by lions as they tried to cross through the Kruger National Park from Mozambique into Northern Province, park officials said on Thursday.
